title.en: Volume 112 Biographies 62: Li Gao, Li Lin, Li Guozhen, Li Huan, Li Ju
title.raw: 卷一百十二 列傳第六十二: 李暠 李麟 李國貞 李峘 李巨 Volume 112 Biographies 62: Li Gao, Li Lin, Li Guozhen, Li Huan, Li Ju

sentences.zh: 李暠族弟齊物齊物子復暠族弟若水

translations.literal: Li Gao's paternal cousin Qi Wu; Qi Wu's son Fu; Li Gao's paternal cousin Ruoshui
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao's paternal cousin Qi Wu; Qi Wu's son Fu; and Li Gao's paternal cousin Ruoshui

sentences.zh: 李麟李國貞子锜

translations.literal: Li Lin; Li Guozhen's son Qi
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin; and Li Guozhen's son Qi

sentences.zh: 李峘弟嶧峴

translations.literal: Li Huan; his younger brothers Yi and Xian
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan; his brothers Yi and Xian

sentences.zh: 李巨子則之

translations.literal: Li Ju's son Zhezhi
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju's son Zhezhi

sentences.zh: 李暠，淮安王神通玄孫，清河王孝節孫也。

translations.literal: Li Gao was a great-great-grandson of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a grandson of Prince of Qinghe Li Xiaojie.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao was a great-grandson of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a grandson of Prince of Qinghe Li Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 暠少孤，事母甚謹。

translations.literal: Gao was orphaned young and served his mother with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Gao lost his father early and attended his mother with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，累轉衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Ruizong he was repeatedly transferred and became Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ruizong he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 丁憂去職，在喪柴毀，家人密親未嘗窺其言笑。

translations.literal: He left office upon bereavement; during mourning he wasted his body through fasting and self-mortification, and even close family members never caught sight of him speaking or smiling.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning and during the funeral period emaciated himself through fasting and self-mortification; even close kin never saw him speak or smile.

sentences.zh: 開元初，授汝州刺史，為政嚴簡，州境肅然。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era he was appointed Prefect of Ru Prefecture; his governance was stern yet spare, and the prefecture became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan period he was appointed prefect of Ru Prefecture; his administration was strict yet economical, and the region became notably orderly.

sentences.zh: 與兄昇弟暈，尤相篤睦，昇等每月自東都省暠，往來微行，州人不之覺，其清慎如此。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Sheng and younger brother Yun he was especially close and harmonious; each month Sheng and the others would come from the Eastern Capital to visit Gao, travelling discreetly so that the people of the prefecture never noticed—such was his discretion and caution.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to his elder brother Sheng and younger brother Yun; each month they would leave the Eastern Capital to visit Gao, travelling so unobtrusively that the people of the prefecture never noticed—such was his probity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 俄入授太常少卿，三遷黃門侍郎，兼太原尹，仍充太原已北諸軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the capital and was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; after three promotions he became Vice Minister of the Secretariat, concurrently Prefect of Taiyuan, and also served as Military Commissioner for all forces north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered court as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted three times to vice minister of the Secretariat, served concurrently as prefect of Taiyuan, and was also military commissioner for all armies north of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太原舊俗，有僧徒以習禪為業，及死不殮，但以屍送近郊以飼鳥獸。

translations.literal: An old custom of Taiyuan had Buddhist monks who made Chan practice their vocation; when they died there was no encoffining—they merely sent the corpse to the outskirts to feed birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan had an old custom whereby monks who devoted themselves to Chan practice, when they died, were not buried but their corpses were taken to the outskirts to feed birds and wild animals.

sentences.zh: 如是積年，土人號其地為「黃坑」。

translations.literal: This went on for years, and the locals called the place the "Yellow Pit."
translations.idiomatic: Year after year this continued, until locals called the place the "Yellow Pit."

sentences.zh: 側有餓狗千數，食死人肉，因侵害幼弱，遠近患之，前後官吏不能禁止。

translations.literal: Beside it were thousands of starving dogs that ate the flesh of the dead; they then preyed on the young and weak, causing distress far and near, and successive officials could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of starving dogs beside it fed on corpses and then attacked children; the trouble spread far and wide, yet successive officials could not put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 暠到官，申明禮憲，期不再犯，發兵捕殺群狗，其風遂革。

translations.literal: When Gao took office he proclaimed ritual regulations and set a term after which the practice would not recur; he sent troops to hunt down and kill the packs of dogs, and the custom was thereby reformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao took office he proclaimed ritual law, fixed a deadline after which the practice must cease, and sent troops to kill the dog packs; the custom was reformed.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉太常卿，旬日，拜工部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; ten days later he was appointed Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he became minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; ten days later he was appointed minister of works and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年正月，制曰：「繼好之義，雖屬邊鄙；

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan an edict stated: "The duty of continuing friendly relations, though it concerns the borderlands;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 733 an edict declared: "The duty of maintaining friendly ties, though it belongs to the frontier;

sentences.zh: 受命以出，必在親賢。

translations.literal: when one receives a commission to go forth, it must fall upon a close kinsman or worthy.
translations.idiomatic: when an envoy is commissioned to depart, he must be a close kinsman or a man of worth.

sentences.zh: 事欲重於當時，禮故崇於殊俗，選眾之舉，無出宗英。

translations.literal: The affair must carry weight for the age, and ritual therefore is exalted toward foreign customs; in choosing from the multitude, none surpasses a clansman of excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The mission must carry weight in its time, and ritual therefore honors foreign custom; in selecting from the many, none surpasses an outstanding member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書李暠，體含柔嘉，識致明允，為公族之領袖，是朝廷之羽儀。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Li Gao, in person gentle and fine, in understanding clear and fair, is a leader among the imperial clansmen and a feathered standard of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Gao combines gentle excellence with clear and sound judgment; he is a leader among the imperial kin and an ornament of the court.

sentences.zh: 金城公主既在蕃中，漢庭公卿非無專對，有懷於遠，夫豈能忘，宜持節充入吐蕃使，準式發遣。

translations.literal: Since Princess Jincheng is already among the Tibetans, the Han court's ministers are not without men who can answer alone; concern for the distant—how could it be forgotten? He should bear credentials as envoy entering Tibet and be dispatched according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Since Princess Jincheng already resides in Tibet, the Han court surely has ministers capable of diplomatic reply; concern for distant lands cannot be set aside. He should go as credentialed envoy to Tibet and be dispatched according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 」以國信物一萬匹、私覿物二千匹，皆雜以五彩遣之。

translations.literal: " Ten thousand bolts of state gifts and two thousand bolts of private audience gifts were all mixed with the five colors and sent with him.
translations.idiomatic: " He was sent with ten thousand bolts of state gifts and two thousand bolts of private gifts, all woven in the five colors.

sentences.zh: 及還，金城公主上言，請以今年九月一日樹碑於赤嶺，定蕃、漢界。

translations.literal: Upon his return, Princess Jincheng submitted a memorial requesting that on the first day of the ninth month of this year a stele be erected at Red Ridge to fix the Tibetan and Han border.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Princess Jincheng petitioned that on the first day of the ninth month a boundary stele be erected at Red Ridge to mark the Tibetan and Han frontier.

sentences.zh: 樹碑之日，詔張守珪、李行袆與吐蕃使莽布支同往觀焉。

translations.literal: On the day the stele was erected, Zhang Shougui, Li Xingwei, and the Tibetan envoy Mangbuzhi were ordered to go together to witness it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the stele was raised, Zhang Shougui and Li Xingwei were ordered to attend with the Tibetan envoy Mangbuzhi.

sentences.zh: 既而吐蕃遣其臣隨漢使分往劍南及河西、磧西，歷告邊州曰：「兩國和好，無相侵掠。

translations.literal: Thereafter Tibet sent its officials to follow the Han envoys separately to Jiannan and Hexi and west of the desert, and everywhere they informed the border prefectures: "The two states are at peace; there shall be no mutual encroachment."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet then sent officials to accompany Han envoys to Jiannan, Hexi, and the western frontier, announcing at each border prefecture: "The two realms are at peace and shall not encroach on one another."

sentences.zh: 」漢使告亦如之。

translations.literal: " The Han envoys proclaimed the same.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han envoys made the same proclamation.

sentences.zh: 以暠奉使稱職，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Because Gao fulfilled his mission with distinction, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gao discharged his embassy with distinction, he was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時吏部告身印與曹印文同，行用參雜，難以區分，暠奏請準司勛兵部印文例，加「官告」兩字，至今行之。

translations.literal: At that time the seal on Ministry of Personnel appointment credentials and the office seal bore the same inscription; in use they were mixed and hard to distinguish. Gao memorialized requesting that, following the precedent of the Ministries of Personnel for Honors and War, the two characters "official appointment" be added—and this practice continues to the present.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the seals on ministry appointment documents and office seals bore identical inscriptions and were easily confused. Gao memorialized that, following the precedent of the ministries of honors and war, the words "official appointment" be added—a practice that continues today.

sentences.zh: 暠風儀秀整，所歷皆以威重見稱，朝廷稱其有宰相之望。

translations.literal: Gao's bearing was elegant and composed; in every post he was praised for dignity and weight, and the court said he had the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's bearing was refined and imposing; wherever he served he was praised for gravitas, and the court regarded him as a man with the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 累封武都縣伯，俄為太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in succession as Baron of Wudu County and soon became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled in succession as Baron of Wudu and soon appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 病卒，年六十余，贈益州大都督。

translations.literal: He died of illness at over sixty years of age and was posthumously made Governor-General of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in his sixties and was posthumously appointed governor-general of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊物，淮安王神通子、鹽州刺史銳孫也。

translations.literal: Qi Wu was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a grandson of Prefect of Yan Prefecture Li Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and grandson of Yan Prefecture prefect Li Rui.

sentences.zh: 齊物無學術，在官嚴整。

translations.literal: Qi Wu had no scholarly learning but in office was stern and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu had little scholarly learning, but in office he was strict and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年後，歷懷、陜二州刺史。

translations.literal: After the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan he served in succession as Prefect of Huai and Shan Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After 736 he served in succession as prefect of Huai and Shan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 齊物天寶初開砥柱之險，以通流運，於石中得古鐵犁鏵，有「平陸」字，因改河北縣為平陸縣，加齊物銀青光祿大夫，為鴻臚卿、河南尹。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era Qi Wu opened the peril of the Dizhu rapids to clear the water transport; in the stone he obtained an ancient iron plowshare with the characters "Pinglu," and therefore changed Hebei County to Pinglu County. Qi Wu was given the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made Director of the Court for Dependencies and Prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign Qi Wu cleared the Dizhu rapids to open river transport; among the rocks he found an ancient iron plowshare inscribed "Pinglu," and renamed Hebei County Pinglu County. He was promoted to silver-gleaming grand master of splendid happiness and appointed director of the court for dependencies and prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 齊物與右相李適之善，適之為林甫所構貶官，齊物坐謫竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Qi Wu was on good terms with the Right Chancellor Li Shizhi; when Shizhi was framed by Li Linfu and demoted, Qi Wu was implicated and banished as Prefect of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was friendly with Right Chancellor Li Shizhi; when Shizhi was framed by Li Linfu and demoted, Qi Wu was implicated and exiled as prefect of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 入為司農、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Agriculture and Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as minister of agriculture and director of the court for dependencies.

sentences.zh: 至德初，拜太子賓客，遷刑部尚書、鳳翔尹、太常卿、京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era he was appointed Household Companion to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Minister of Justice, Prefect of Fengxiang, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhide reign he was appointed household companion to the heir apparent, then rose to minister of justice, prefect of Fengxiang, minister of the court of imperial sacrifices, and prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 為政發官吏陰事，以察為能，於物少恩，而清廉自飭，人吏莫敢抵犯。

translations.literal: In governing he exposed officials' hidden affairs and took keen scrutiny as his ability; he showed little kindness toward others, yet disciplined himself in integrity and purity, and neither clerks nor commoners dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he exposed officials' secret misconduct and prided himself on sharp scrutiny; he was sparing of mercy yet scrupulously self-restrained in integrity, and neither subordinates nor the public dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 晚年除太子太傅、兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: In his later years he was appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was appointed grand tutor to the heir apparent and concurrently director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 上元二年五月卒，輟朝一日。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth month of the second year of Shangyuan; court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of 761; the court suspended audiences for one day.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「故金紫光祿大夫、太子太傅、兼宗正卿齊物，宗室珪璋，士林楨幹，清廉獨斷，剛毅不群。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The late Gold-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan Court Qi Wu was a jade scepter of the imperial clan and a main pillar of the scholarly world—pure and incorruptible, decisive alone, firm and resolute beyond the common run."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The late Gold-Gleaming Grand Master Qi Wu, grand tutor to the heir apparent and concurrent director of the imperial clan court, was a jewel of the imperial house and a pillar of the scholarly world—incorruptible and decisive, resolute beyond the common run."

sentences.zh: 歷踐周行，備經中外，威名益振，忠效彌彰。

translations.literal: He trod the full circuit of offices and experienced both central and regional service; his renown for authority grew ever greater and his loyal service ever clearer.
translations.idiomatic: He served through the full range of offices, both at court and in the provinces; his reputation for authority grew and his loyal service shone ever brighter.

sentences.zh: 三尹神州，一登會府，擒奸掩鉤距之術，恤獄正喉舌之官。

translations.literal: Three times he governed the imperial metropolis, once he ascended the office of the metropolitan prefecture; he seized the wicked and concealed the arts of hook and distance; he showed compassion in prisons and rectified the office of the mouth and tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Thrice he governed the capital region, once he headed the metropolitan prefecture; he exposed wrongdoing and mastered subtle stratagems, showed compassion in prisons, and set right the censorial offices.

sentences.zh: 遂令調護儲闈，再登師傅，從容賓友，師長官僚。

translations.literal: Thus he was ordered to attend and nurture the heir's quarters, twice ascended as tutor, at ease as companion to the heir, and teacher and elder to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was then charged with overseeing the heir's household, twice served as tutor, was a steady companion to the heir, and guided the officials.

sentences.zh: 桑榆之時，壯誌逾勵；

translations.literal: In the mulberry-and-sunset years his stalwart will grew only more ardent;
translations.idiomatic: In his twilight years his resolve grew only stronger;

sentences.zh: 松柏之性，晚歲常堅。

translations.literal: the nature of pine and cypress—late in life ever firm.
translations.idiomatic: like pine and cypress, firm to the end.

sentences.zh: 天不慭遺，奄然殂謝，念親感舊，深軫於懷。

translations.literal: Heaven was not kind in leaving him; suddenly he passed away. Thinking of kin and moved by old ties, the heart is deeply stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was not kind to leave him; he has suddenly passed away. Remembering kinship and old ties, our hearts are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 宜錫寵章，載光營魄。

translations.literal: He should be granted favor and an honorific title to shed glory upon his spirit in the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Let favor and posthumous honors be granted to bring glory to his departed spirit.

sentences.zh: 可贈太子太師。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed grand tutor to the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 子復，字初陽，以父廕累官至江陵府司錄。

translations.literal: His son Fu, style name Chuyang, through his father's privilege of succession rose in office to Registrar of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu, courtesy name Chuyang, rose through his father's yin privilege to registrar of Jiangling prefecture.

sentences.zh: 精曉吏道，衛伯玉厚遇之，府中之事，多以咨委。

translations.literal: He was thoroughly versed in the ways of clerical administration; Wei Boyu treated him generously, and most affairs of the prefecture were entrusted to his consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert in administrative practice; Wei Boyu favored him highly, and most prefectural affairs were referred to him.

sentences.zh: 性苛刻，為伯玉所信，奏為江陵縣令，遷少尹，歷饒州、蘇州刺史，皆著政聲。

translations.literal: His nature was harsh; trusted by Boyu, he was memorialized as Magistrate of Jiangling County, promoted to Vice Prefect, and served in succession as Prefect of Rao and Su Prefectures—all with noted reputation in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh by nature, he won Boyu's trust, was recommended as magistrate of Jiangling, promoted to vice prefect, and served as prefect of Rao and Su—winning renown for his governance at each post.

sentences.zh: 李希烈背叛，荊南節度張伯儀數出兵，為希烈所敗，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, Zhang Boyi of the Jingnan command repeatedly sent troops and was defeated by Xilie; the court was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, Jingnan military commissioner Zhang Boyi repeatedly took the field and was defeated; the court grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 以復久在江陵，得軍民心，復方在母喪，起為江陵少尹、兼御史中丞，充節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Because Fu had long been in Jiangling and won the hearts of soldiers and people, though he was in mourning for his mother he was summoned to serve as Vice Prefect of Jiangling and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, acting as campaigning marshal of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu had long served at Jiangling and won army and populace alike, he was summoned from mourning for his mother to be vice prefect of Jiangling and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, serving as campaigning marshal under the military commission.

sentences.zh: 伯儀既受代，以復為容州刺史、兼御史中丞，充本管招討使，加檢校常侍。

translations.literal: After Boyi was relieved, Fu was made Prefect of Rong Prefecture and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, charged as pacification commissioner of the circuit, with the added title of acting regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyi was relieved, Fu was appointed prefect of Rong, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of the circuit, with the added title of acting regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 先時西原叛亂，前後經略使征討反者，獲其人皆沒為官奴婢，配作坊重役，復乃令訪其親屬，悉歸還之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the western plains rebelled, successive frontier commissioners who campaigned against the rebels took captives and made them all state slaves and bondmaids, assigned to workshops for heavy labor. Fu then ordered their kin sought out and all returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the western plains rebelled, frontier commissioners who suppressed the uprising enslaved captives for heavy workshop labor. Fu had their kin traced and returned them all to their families.

sentences.zh: 在容州三歲，南人安悅。

translations.literal: During three years in Rong Prefecture the southern people were peaceful and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After three years at Rong, the southern peoples were tranquil and content.

sentences.zh: 遷廣州刺史、兼御史大夫、嶺南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Guang Prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner and Observer of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Guang, concurrent censor-in-chief, and military commissioner and observer of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 會安南經略使高正平、張應相次卒官，其下參佐偏裨李元度、胡懷義等阻兵，黷亂州縣，奸贓狼藉。

translations.literal: It happened that the Annan frontier commissioners Gao Zhengping and Zhang Ying died in office one after another; their subordinate staff officers and junior generals Li Yuandu, Hu Huaiyi, and others obstructed the army, wantonly disturbed prefectures and counties, and left corruption in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: When Annan commissioners Gao Zhengping and Zhang Ying died in succession, subordinates Li Yuandu, Hu Huaiyi, and others held troops unlawfully, ravaged the prefectures, and left corruption everywhere.

sentences.zh: 復誘懷義杖殺之，奏元度流於荒裔。

translations.literal: Fu lured Huaiyi and had him beaten to death, then memorialized that Yuandu be exiled to the remote borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Fu lured Hu Huaiyi and had him beaten to death, then memorialized that Li Yuandu be exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又勸導百姓，令變茅屋為瓦舍。

translations.literal: He also exhorted and guided the people to change thatched huts into tiled houses.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the people to replace thatched huts with tiled dwellings.

sentences.zh: 瓊州久陷於蠻獠中，復累遣使喻之，因奏置瓊州都督府以綏撫之。

translations.literal: Qiong Prefecture had long been lost among the Man and Liao; Fu repeatedly sent envoys to instruct them and memorialized to establish the Qiong Area Command to pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong Prefecture had long fallen among tribal peoples; Fu repeatedly sent envoys to win them over and memorialized to establish an area command at Qiong to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 復曉於政道，所在稱理，征拜宗正卿，加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Fu was versed in the ways of governance; wherever he served he was praised for good order. He was summoned and appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court, with the added title of acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in governance, he was praised for good order wherever he served. He was summoned as director of the imperial clan court with the added title of acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未一歲，會華州節度李元諒卒，以復為華州刺史、潼關防禦鎮國軍使，仍檢校戶部尚書，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Within less than a year, when Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture Li Yuanliang died, Fu was made Prefect of Hua, Defender of Tong Pass and Commissioner of the Army that Stabilizes the State, still acting Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, when Hua military commissioner Li Yuanliang died, Fu was appointed prefect of Hua, defender of Tong Pass and commissioner of the army that stabilizes the state, with the added titles of acting minister of revenue and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，鄭滑節度使李融卒，軍中潰亂，以復檢校兵部尚書，兼滑州刺史、義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察營田等使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan, Military Commissioner of Zheng and Hua Li Rong died and the army fell into disorder; Fu was made acting Minister of War, concurrent Prefect of Hua Prefecture, Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army, Observer of Zheng and Hua, Commissioner of Military Farms, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 794, Zheng-Hua military commissioner Li Rong died and the army fell into disorder; Fu was appointed acting minister of war, concurrent prefect of Hua, military commissioner of the Yicheng army, observer of Zheng and Hua, commissioner of military farms, and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 復到任，置營田數百頃，以資軍食，不率於民，眾皆悅之。

translations.literal: When Fu arrived he established several hundred qing of military farms to supply army provisions, without imposing on the people; all were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he established several hundred qing of military farms to supply the army without burdening the populace, and all were pleased.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was given the added title of acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 796 he was given the added title of acting left vice director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月卒官，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year he died in office at fifty-nine years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 797 he died in office at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈司空。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for three days; he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended for three days; he was posthumously appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 賻布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: Funerary gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were given in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were granted in due measure.

sentences.zh: 復久典方面，積財頗甚，為時所譏。

translations.literal: Fu had long governed frontier circuits and amassed considerable wealth, for which his age criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: Having long governed frontier circuits, he amassed considerable wealth and was criticized by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 李麟，皇室之疏屬，太宗之從孫也。

translations.literal: Li Lin was a distant member of the imperial house, a grandnephew of Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin was a distant kinsman of the imperial house, a grandnephew of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父浚，開元初置十道按察使，精選吏才，以浚為潤州刺史、江南東道按察使。

translations.literal: His father Jun, when at the beginning of Kaiyuan the ten-circuit investigation commissioners were established and official talent was carefully selected, was made Prefect of Run Prefecture and Investigation Commissioner of the Jiangnan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun, when the ten-circuit investigation commissioners were established early in Kaiyuan and official talent was carefully chosen, was appointed prefect of Run and investigation commissioner of the Jiangnan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 轉虢潞二州刺史，益州大都督府長史、攝御史大夫、劍南節度按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Guo and Lu Prefectures, Chief Administrator of the Governor-General's Office of Yizhou, acting Censor-in-Chief, and Investigation Commissioner of the Jiannan Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Guo and Lu, chief administrator of the Yizhou governor-general's office, acting censor-in-chief, and investigation commissioner of the Jiannan military commission.

sentences.zh: 所歷以誠信待物，稱為良吏。

translations.literal: In every post he treated others with sincerity and trust and was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he treated others with sincerity and trust and was acclaimed as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 八年卒，贈戶部尚書，謚曰誠。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue; his posthumous title was Sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 720 and was posthumously appointed minister of revenue with the posthumous name Sincere.

sentences.zh: 麟以父任補職，累授京兆府戶曹。

translations.literal: Lin entered office through his father's privilege of succession and was repeatedly appointed Household Section Chief of Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lin entered service through his father's yin privilege and rose to household section chief of Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年，舉宗室異能，轉殿中侍御史，歷戶部、考功、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan he was nominated among the imperial clan for unusual ability, transferred to Attendant Censor within the Palace, and served in succession as Vice Director in the Ministries of Revenue, Personnel for Honors, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 734 he was nominated from the imperial clan for exceptional ability, became palace attendant censor, and served as vice director in the ministries of revenue, honors, and personnel.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，遷郎中，尋改諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was promoted to Director; soon after he was changed to Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In 742 he was promoted to director; soon after he was appointed remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 五載，充河西、隴右、磧西等道黜陟使，稱旨，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioner for the Hexi, Longyou, and western desert circuits; finding favor, he was promoted to Attendant within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 746 he served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Hexi, Longyou, and the western desert circuits; finding favor, he was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 七載，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 748 he was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 同列楊國忠專權，不悅麟同職，宰臣奏麟以本官權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: His colleague Yang Guozhong monopolized power and was displeased that Lin shared the same rank; the chief ministers memorialized that Lin, in his present office, should act as temporary overseer of the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Yang Guozhong monopolized power and disliked sharing rank with Lin; the chief ministers had Lin, in his present office, temporarily oversee the civil examination.

sentences.zh: 俄而國忠為御史大夫，麟復本官。

translations.literal: Soon Guozhong became Censor-in-Chief and Lin returned to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guozhong became censor-in-chief and Lin resumed his original post.

sentences.zh: 十一載，遷銀青光祿大夫、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 he was promoted to silver-gleaming grand master of splendid happiness and chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月，以本官出為河東太守、河東道采訪使，為政清簡，民吏稱之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, in his present office he went out as Prefect of Hedong and Investigation Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit; his governance was pure and spare, and people and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 755 he left court as prefect of Hedong and investigation commissioner of the Hedong circuit; his administration was pure and economical, and officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，祿山構逆，朝廷以麟儒者，恐非禦侮之用，仍以將軍呂崇賁代還。

translations.literal: That winter Lushan plotted rebellion; the court, considering Lin a Confucian scholar, feared he was not fit to repel insult, and still sent General Lü Chongben to replace him and return.
translations.idiomatic: That winter when Lushan rebelled, the court regarded Lin as a scholar unsuited to military defense and sent General Lü Chongben to replace him.

sentences.zh: 復以祭酒歸朝，賜爵渭源縣男。

translations.literal: He again returned to court as Chancellor of the Directorate and was granted the title Baron of Weiyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as chancellor of the directorate and was ennobled as Baron of Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，玄宗幸蜀，麟奔赴行在。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu; Lin hurried to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, when Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu, Lin hurried to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 既至成都，拜戶部侍郎，兼左丞。

translations.literal: Once he reached Chengdu he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chengdu he was appointed vice minister of revenue and concurrent left vice director.

sentences.zh: 遷憲部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 至德二年正月，拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhide he was appointed Associate Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 757 he was appointed associate grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 時扈從宰相韋見素、房琯、崔渙已赴鳳翔，俄而崔圓繼去，玄宗以麟宗室子，獨留之，行在百司，麟總攝其事。

translations.literal: At that time the accompanying chancellors Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan had already gone to Fengxiang; soon Cui Yuan followed. Emperor Xuanzong, because Lin was of the imperial clan, kept him alone; of the hundred offices at the mobile court, Lin took overall charge of their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The accompanying chancellors Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan had already gone to Fengxiang, and Cui Yuan soon followed. Because Lin was of the imperial clan, Xuanzong kept him alone to oversee all affairs of the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，從上皇還京，策勛行賞，加金紫光祿大夫、刑部尚書、同中書門下三品，進封褒國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he followed the Retired Emperor back to the capital; merits were assessed and rewards given. He was given Gold-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, and Third Rank of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Bao State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he accompanied the retired emperor back to the capital; for his merit he was given gold-gleaming grand master, minister of justice, and third rank of the secretariat-chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Bao.

sentences.zh: 李國貞，淮安王神通子、淄川王孝同之曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Guozhen was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a great-grandson of Prince of Zichuan Li Xiaotong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and great-grandson of Prince of Zichuan Li Xiaotong.

sentences.zh: 父廣業，劍州長史。

translations.literal: His father Guangye was Chief Administrator of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangye was chief administrator of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 國貞本名若幽，性剛正，有吏才，歷安定、扶風錄事參軍，皆稱職。

translations.literal: Guozhen's original name was Ruoyou; his nature was firm and upright and he had talent for administration. He served as Recording Advisor in Anding and Fufeng and in each was praised as competent.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's original name was Ruoyou; upright and capable in administration, he served as recording advisor in Anding and Fufeng and was praised as competent at each post.

sentences.zh: 乾元中累遷長安令，尋拜河南尹。

translations.literal: During the Qianyuan era he was repeatedly promoted to Magistrate of Chang'an and soon appointed Prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan reign he rose to magistrate of Chang'an and soon became prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 會史思明逼城，元帥李光弼東保河陽，國貞領官吏寓於陜。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming pressed the city, the commander Li Guangbi held Hedong to the east, and Guozhen led officials and clerks to lodge in Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming besieged the city, commander Li Guangbi withdrew east to defend Heyang, and Guozhen led officials to lodge at Shan.

sentences.zh: 數月，征為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Several months later he was summoned as Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was summoned as prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 上元初，改成都尹、兼御史大夫，充劍南節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he was changed to Prefect of Chengdu, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and charged as Military Commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan reign he was appointed prefect of Chengdu, concurrent censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中監。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as director of the palace domestic service.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，遷戶部尚書、兼御史大夫，持節充朔方、鎮西、北庭、興平、陳鄭等節度行營兵馬及河中節度都統處置使，鎮於絳，賜名國貞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials as overall commander and disposition commissioner for the campaigning armies of the Shuofang, Western Frontier, Northern Court, Xingping, Chen-Zheng, and other military commissions and for the Hedong military commission, stationed at Jiang; he was granted the name Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 759 he became minister of revenue and concurrent censor-in-chief, with credentials as overall commander of the Shuofang, western frontier, northern court, Xingping, Chen-Zheng, and related campaigning forces and disposition commissioner for Hedong, stationed at Jiang; he was granted the name Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 既至，又加充管內河中、晉、絳、慈、隰、沁等州觀察處置等使，余並如故。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was further charged as Observer and Disposition Commissioner for Hedong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, Qin, and other prefectures within his circuit; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was also made observer and disposition commissioner for Hedong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, Qin, and other prefectures under his authority; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 國貞既至絳，屬軍中素無儲積，百姓饑饉，難為聚斂，將士等糧賜多闕。

translations.literal: After Guozhen reached Jiang, the army had long had no stores, the people suffered famine, levies were hard to collect, and soldiers' grain and stipends were largely lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen reached Jiang, the army had no reserves, the people were starving, taxes could scarcely be raised, and soldiers' rations and pay were largely unpaid.

sentences.zh: 國貞頻以狀聞，未報。

translations.literal: Guozhen repeatedly reported the situation in memorials but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen repeatedly memorialized the court but received no response.

sentences.zh: 軍中喧喧怨讀，左右以告國貞，國貞喻之曰：「軍將何苦如是，已為奏聞，終有所給。

translations.literal: The army clamored with resentment; his attendants reported this to Guozhen, and Guozhen instructed them: "Generals, why suffer so? I have already memorialized; in the end there will be provisions."
translations.idiomatic: The troops grew loud with complaint; when his staff reported this, Guozhen told them: "Officers, why be so distressed? I have already memorialized the throne; supplies will come in time."

sentences.zh: 」信宿軍亂，攻國貞，夜燒衙城門。

translations.literal: " Within a day and night the army mutinied, attacked Guozhen, and at night burned the yamen city gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Within a day and night the army mutinied, attacked him, and burned the government gate that night.

sentences.zh: 國貞莫知所圖，左右勸國貞棄城遁去，國貞曰：「吾銜命為將，不能靖難，安可棄城乎！

translations.literal: Guozhen did not know what to do; his attendants urged him to abandon the city and flee. Guozhen said: "I bear a commission as general; if I cannot quell disorder, how can I abandon the city!"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was at a loss; his attendants urged him to abandon the city and flee. He said: "I hold a general's commission; if I cannot restore order, how can I abandon the city!"

sentences.zh: 」左右固勸回避，乃隱於州獄，詐負縲紲。

translations.literal: " His attendants firmly urged him to withdraw; he then hid in the prefectural prison and pretended to wear fetters.
translations.idiomatic: " His staff pressed him to hide; he concealed himself in the prefectural jail and feigned imprisonment in chains.

sentences.zh: 會國貞麾下為賊所擒，因指所在，遂於獄中執國貞，將害之，國貞曰：「軍中乏糧，已有陳請，人不堪賦，予無負於將士耳。

translations.literal: It happened that one of Guozhen's subordinates was seized by the mutineers and pointed out his whereabouts; they then seized Guozhen in the prison and were about to kill him. Guozhen said: "The army lacks grain; I have already memorialized. The people cannot bear levies—I have done no wrong to the officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: When one of his men was captured by the mutineers and revealed his hiding place, they seized him in the jail and were about to kill him. Guozhen said: "The army lacks grain and I have already petitioned the throne. The people cannot bear more levies—I have wronged no soldier."

sentences.zh: 」眾引退。

translations.literal: " The crowd withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " The mob withdrew.

sentences.zh: 突將王元振獨曰：「今日之事，豈須問焉！

translations.literal: The assault officer Wang Yuanzhen alone said: "Today's affair—why need there be any questioning!"
translations.idiomatic: Assault officer Wang Yuanzhen alone cried: "For today's business, what need is there to ask!"

sentences.zh: 」抽刀害國貞及二男、三大將。

translations.literal: " He drew his blade and killed Guozhen, his two sons, and three great generals.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his sword and killed Guozhen, his two sons, and three senior generals.

sentences.zh: 國貞有風采，清白守法，為政急於操下，時論以辨吏稱之。

translations.literal: Guozhen had presence and bearing, was pure and law-abiding in office, and in governing was urgent in controlling subordinates; contemporary opinion praised him as a discerning official.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen had presence and bearing, kept himself pure and law-abiding, and governed with stern control of subordinates; contemporaries praised him as a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 追贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor-General of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed governor-general of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子锜，以父廕貞元中累至湖、杭二州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Qi, through his father's privilege of succession, during the Zhenyuan era rose in succession to Prefect of Hu and Hang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, through his father's yin privilege, rose during the Zhenyuan reign to prefect of Hu and Hang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 多以寶貨賂李齊運，由是遷潤州刺史兼鹽鐵使，持積財進奉，以結恩澤，德宗甚寵之。

translations.literal: He largely used treasures and goods to bribe Li Qiyun; thereby he was transferred to Prefect of Run Prefecture and concurrent Salt and Iron Commissioner, amassing wealth to present in tribute to win favor, and Emperor Dezong greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished treasures on Li Qiyun and was promoted to prefect of Run and concurrent salt and iron commissioner; he amassed wealth for tribute to court favor, and Emperor Dezong favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 锜恃恩驕恣，有浙西人布衣崔善貞詣闕上封，論锜罪狀，而德宗械送賜锜，锜遂坑殺善貞，天下切齒。

translations.literal: Qi relied on favor and was arrogant and unrestrained. A commoner of western Zhe named Cui Shanzhen went to the palace gate with a sealed memorial denouncing Qi's crimes, but Dezong had him shackled and sent as a gift to Qi; Qi then buried him alive, and all under heaven gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on imperial favor, Qi grew arrogant. A commoner of western Zhe, Cui Shanzhen, submitted a sealed memorial at court denouncing his crimes, but Dezong had him shackled and sent to Qi, who buried him alive; the empire seethed with outrage.

sentences.zh: 乃增置兵額，選善弓矢者聚之一營，名曰「挽硬隨身」；

translations.literal: He then increased troop quotas and selected men skilled with bow and arrow, gathering them in one camp called "Hard-Drawing Personal Guard";
translations.idiomatic: He then expanded his forces and gathered skilled archers in one camp called the "Hard-Drawing Personal Guard";

sentences.zh: 以胡、奚雜類虬須者為一將，名曰「蕃落健兒」。

translations.literal: he made one commander of mixed Hu and Xi types with bristling beards, named "Frontier Elite Warriors."
translations.idiomatic: and formed another unit of Hu and Xi men with bristling beards under a commander called the "Frontier Elite Warriors."

sentences.zh: 德宗復於潤州置鎮海軍，以锜為節度使，罷其鹽鐵使務。

translations.literal: Dezong again established the Zhenhai Army at Run Prefecture and made Qi its military commissioner, removing his salt and iron duties.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong then established the Zhenhai army at Run and made Qi its military commissioner, relieving him of his salt and iron post.

sentences.zh: 锜雖罷其利權，且得節度，反狀未發。

translations.literal: Although Qi lost his profit-making authority, he still gained a military commission, and his rebellious intent had not yet surfaced.
translations.idiomatic: Though Qi lost his lucrative salt monopoly, he gained a military commission, and his rebellion had not yet broken out.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位已二年，諸道倔強者入朝，而锜不自安，亦請入朝，乃拜锜左僕射。

translations.literal: Two years after Emperor Xianzong took the throne, the stubborn military commissioners of the circuits came to court; Qi was ill at ease and also requested to come to court, and he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after Xianzong's accession, recalcitrant regional commanders came to court; uneasy, Qi also requested an audience and was appointed left vice director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 锜乃署判官王淡為留後。

translations.literal: Qi then appointed his judicial officer Wang Dan as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi appointed his judicial officer Wang Dan acting commissioner in his absence.

sentences.zh: 既而遷延發期，淡與中使頻喻之，不悅，遂諷將士以給冬衣日殺淡而食之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he delayed his departure; Dan and the palace envoy repeatedly urged him, displeasing him, and he then incited the soldiers on the day winter clothing was issued to kill Dan and eat him.
translations.idiomatic: He then delayed departure; when Dan and the palace envoy repeatedly urged him, he grew angry and incited the troops, on the day winter clothing was issued, to kill Dan and devour him.

sentences.zh: 監軍使聞亂，遣衙將趙锜慰喻，又臠食之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor heard of the disorder and sent yamen general Zhao Qi to console and instruct them; they carved him up and ate him as well.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor sent yamen general Zhao Qi to calm the troops; they butchered and ate him too.

sentences.zh: 復以兵註中使之頸，锜佯驚救解之，囚於別館。

translations.literal: They again held weapons to the palace envoy's neck; Qi feigned alarm and rescued him, then imprisoned him in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: They then held blades to the envoy's throat; Qi feigned alarm, "rescued" him, and imprisoned him in a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 遂稱兵，飾五劍，分授管內鎮將，令殺刺史。

translations.literal: He then raised troops, adorned five swords, and distributed them to the garrison commanders within his circuit, ordering them to kill the prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He then took up arms, had five swords ornamented, and gave them to garrison commanders throughout his circuit with orders to kill the prefects.

sentences.zh: 於是常州刺史顏防用客李雲謀，矯制傳檄於蘇、杭、湖、睦等州，遂殺其鎮將李深；

translations.literal: Thereupon Chang Prefecture Prefect Yan Fang, using the plan of his guest Li Yun, forged an edict and circulated a proclamation to Su, Hang, Hu, Mu, and other prefectures, and thus killed his garrison commander Li Shen;
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou prefect Yan Fang, following his retainer Li Yun's plan, forged an edict and circulated a call to Su, Hang, Hu, Mu, and other prefectures, and killed garrison commander Li Shen;

sentences.zh: 湖州辛秘亦殺其鎮將趙惟忠；

translations.literal: Huzhou's Xin Mi also killed his garrison commander Zhao Weizhong;
translations.idiomatic: at Huzhou, Xin Mi also killed garrison commander Zhao Weizhong;

sentences.zh: 而蘇州刺史李素為鎮將姚誌安所系，釘於船舷，生致於锜，未至而锜敗，得免。

translations.literal: while Suzhou Prefect Li Su was bound by garrison commander Yao Zhi'an, nailed to the ship's side, and sent alive to Qi; before he arrived Qi was defeated, and Su was spared.
translations.idiomatic: while Suzhou prefect Li Su was seized by garrison commander Yao Zhi'an, nailed to a ship's side, and sent alive toward Qi; before arrival Qi was defeated, and Li Su was spared.

sentences.zh: 初，锜以宣州富饒，有並吞之意，遣兵馬使張子良、李奉仙、田少卿領兵三千分略宣、池等州。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Xuancheng Prefecture was rich, Qi had intended to swallow it and sent military commissioners Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing leading three thousand troops to overrun Xuancheng, Chi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, coveting the wealth of Xuancheng, Qi sent military commissioners Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing with three thousand men to overrun Xuancheng, Chi, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三將夙有向順誌，而锜甥裴行立亦思向順，其密謀多決於行立，乃回戈趣城，執锜於幕，縋而出之，斬於闕下，年六十七。

translations.literal: The three generals had long wished to turn loyal; Qi's nephew Pei Xingli also wished to turn loyal, and their secret plans were largely decided by Xingli. They then turned their blades toward the city, seized Qi in his tent, lowered him by rope outside, and beheaded him below the gate; he was sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanders had long wished to submit; Qi's nephew Pei Xingli also favored loyalty, and their plot was largely his. They turned back toward the city, seized Qi in his tent, lowered him by rope, and beheaded him before the gate at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其「挽硬」、「蕃落」將士，或投井自縊，紛紛枕藉而死者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: His "Hard-Drawing" and "Frontier Elite" officers and soldiers, some throwing themselves into wells or hanging themselves, lay piled dead beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men of his Hard-Drawing and Frontier Elite units threw themselves into wells or hanged themselves; the dead lay piled beyond count.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭絪等議锜所坐，親疏未定，乃召兵部郎中蔣武問曰：「詔罪李锜一房，當是大功內耶？

translations.literal: Chief ministers Zheng Yin and others discussed the degree of Qi's guilt and whether kin near or far were implicated; they summoned Bureau Director of the Ministry of War Jiang Wu and asked: "If the edict punishes one household of Li Qi, should that be within the greater merit mourning grade?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Zheng Yin and others debated the scope of punishment for Qi's kin and summoned Ministry of War bureau director Jiang Wu, asking: "If the edict punishes one household of Li Qi, should that fall within the greater-merit mourning circle?"

sentences.zh: 」武曰：「大功是锜堂兄弟，即淮安王神通之下，淮安有大功於國，不可以孽孫而上累。

translations.literal: " Wu said: "Greater merit covers Qi's paternal cousins, that is, the line below Prince Huai'an Li Shentong. Huai'an rendered great merit to the state; one cannot let a rebellious descendant implicate him upward."
translations.idiomatic: " Wu replied: "Greater merit would implicate Qi's paternal cousins—the line of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong. Huai'an rendered great service to the state; a rebellious descendant must not drag him down."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「锜親兄弟從坐否？

translations.literal: " They asked again: "Are Qi's full brothers to suffer joint punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: " They asked further: "Should Qi's full brothers be punished with him?"

sentences.zh: 」武曰：「锜親兄弟是若幽之子，若幽有死王事之功，如令锜兄弟從坐，若幽即宜削籍，亦所未安。

translations.literal: " Wu said: "Qi's full brothers are sons of Ruoyou; Ruoyou died in service to the throne. If Qi's brothers are punished jointly, Ruoyou ought to be struck from the registers—which would also be unsettling."
translations.idiomatic: " Wu said: "Qi's full brothers are sons of Ruoyou, who died in the ruler's service. To punish the brothers would require striking Ruoyou from the registers—which would also be unjust."

sentences.zh: 」宰相頗以為然，故誅锜詔下，唯止元惡一房而已。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers largely agreed; therefore when the edict executing Qi was issued, it stopped at the chief villain's household alone.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers agreed; when the execution edict was issued, only the chief villain's household was punished.

sentences.zh: 李峘，太宗第三子吳王恪之孫。

translations.literal: Li Huan was a grandson of Emperor Taizong's third son, Prince of Wu Li Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was a grandson of Prince of Wu Li Ke, the third son of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 恪第三子琨生信安王祎，祎生三子：峘、嶧、峴。

translations.literal: Ke's third son Kun begot Prince of Xin'an Li Yi; Yi begot three sons: Huan, Yi, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's third son Kun fathered Prince of Xin'an Li Yi, who had three sons: Huan, Yi, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 峘誌行修立，天寶中為南宮郎，歷典諸曹十余年。

translations.literal: Huan's will and conduct were cultivated and upright; in the Tianbao era he was a Southern Palace gentleman and for more than ten years presided over various bureaus in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's conduct was upright and cultivated; during Tianbao he served in the Southern Palace and for more than ten years headed various bureaus in turn.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀得禮，服闋，以郡王子例封趙國公。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he grieved and wasted himself according to ritual; when mourning ended, by the precedent for sons of princes of commanderies he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father he observed the rites with proper grief; when mourning ended he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao by the precedent for commandery princes' sons.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠秉政，郎官不附己者悉出於外，峘自考功郎中出為睢陽太守。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong held power, all gentlemen of the palace who did not attach to him were sent out to the regions; Huan left his post as Director of the Bureau of Personnel for Honors and went out as Prefect of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong held power, palace officials who would not attach to him were sent to the provinces; Huan left his post as director of the bureau of honors and became prefect of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 尋而弟峴出為魏郡太守，兄弟夾河典郡，皆以理行稱。

translations.literal: Soon his younger brother Xian went out as Prefect of Wei Commandery; the brothers governed prefectures on opposite banks of the river and were both praised for orderly administration.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his brother Xian became prefect of Wei commandery; the brothers governed facing prefectures on opposite banks of the Yellow River and were both praised for good governance.

sentences.zh: 十四載，入計京師。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered the capital to report.
translations.idiomatic: In 755 he went to the capital on administrative review.

sentences.zh: 屬祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，峘奔赴行在，除武部侍郎，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Lushan's rebellion occurred, Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu; Huan hurried to the mobile court and was made Vice Minister of War and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lushan rebellion broke out and Xuanzong fled to Shu, Huan hurried to the mobile court and was appointed vice minister of war and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 俄拜蜀郡太守、劍南節度采訪使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Shu Commandery and Investigation Commissioner of the Jiannan Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Shu commandery and investigation commissioner of the Jiannan military commission.

sentences.zh: 上皇在成都，健兒郭千仞夜謀亂，上皇禦玄英樓招諭，不從，峘與六軍兵馬使陳玄禮等平之，以功加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was at Chengdu when the stalwart Guo Qianren plotted rebellion by night; the Retired Emperor mounted the Mysterious Glory Tower to summon and instruct them, but they would not obey. Huan, with the Six Armies' military commissioner Chen Xuanli and others, quelled it; for his merit he was given Gold-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu the retired emperor faced a night mutiny led by stalwart Guo Qianren; when summons from the Mysterious Glory Tower failed, Huan and Six Armies commissioner Chen Xuanli quelled it; for this he was given gold-gleaming grand master.

sentences.zh: 時峴為鳳翔太守，匡翊肅宗，兄弟俱效勛力。

translations.literal: At that time Xian was Prefect of Fengxiang, supporting and assisting Emperor Suzong; the brothers both rendered meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xian was prefect of Fengxiang, supporting Emperor Suzong; both brothers rendered distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 從上皇還京，為戶部尚書，峴為御史大夫，兼京兆尹，封梁國公。

translations.literal: Following the Retired Emperor back to the capital, he became Minister of Revenue; Xian became Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Prefect of Jingzhao, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital with the retired emperor, he became minister of revenue; Xian became censor-in-chief and concurrent prefect of Jingzhao and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同制封公。

translations.literal: The brothers were enfeoffed as dukes by the same edict.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were enfeoffed as dukes in the same edict.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，兼御史大夫，持節都統淮南、江南、江西節度、宣慰、觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan he was concurrent Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials as overall commander of the Huainan, Jiangnan, and Jiangxi military commissions and as Pacification, Observation, and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan reign he was concurrent censor-in-chief with credentials as overall commander of Huainan, Jiangnan, and Jiangxi and as pacification, observation, and disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，以宋州刺史劉展握兵河南，有異志，乃陽拜展淮南節度使，而密詔揚州長史鄧景山與峘圖之。

translations.literal: In the second year, because Song Prefecture Prefect Liu Zhan held troops in Henan and harbored divergent intent, he was openly appointed Military Commissioner of Huainan while a secret edict ordered Yangzhou Chief Administrator Deng Jingshan and Huan to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: In 759, because Song prefect Liu Zhan held troops in Henan and harbored disloyal intent, he was openly made Huainan military commissioner while a secret edict ordered Yangzhou chief administrator Deng Jingshan and Huan to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 時展徒黨方強，既受詔，即以兵渡淮。

translations.literal: At that time Zhan's faction was strong; once he received the edict he immediately crossed the Huai with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's faction was then powerful; once he received the appointment he immediately crossed the Huai with his army.

sentences.zh: 景山、峘拒之壽春，為展所敗。

translations.literal: Jingshan and Huan resisted him at Shouchun and were defeated by Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan and Huan resisted at Shouchun and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 峘走渡江，保丹陽，坐貶袁州司馬。

translations.literal: Huan fled across the river and held Danyang; he was demoted as punishment to Military Advisor of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled south across the Yangzi and held Danyang; he was demoted to military advisor of Yuan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，病卒於貶所，追贈揚州大都督，官給遞乘，護柩還京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying he died of illness at his place of demotion; he was posthumously made Governor-General of Yang Prefecture, official relay transport was provided, and his coffin was escorted back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 he died of illness in exile; he was posthumously appointed governor-general of Yangzhou, official relay transport was provided, and his coffin was escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，峘為戶部尚書，峴為吏部尚書、知政事，嶧為戶部侍郎、銀青光祿大夫，兄弟同居長興裏第，門列三戟，兩國公門十六戟，一、三品門十二戟，榮耀冠時。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huan was Minister of Revenue, Xian was Minister of Personnel and handled government affairs, and Yi was Vice Minister of Revenue and Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; the brothers dwelt together in a mansion in Changxing Lane, their gate bearing three halberds—sixteen for two dukes' gates, twelve for first- and third-rank gates—glory surpassing the age.
translations.idiomatic: At their height Huan was minister of revenue, Xian minister of personnel and chief counselor, and Yi vice minister of revenue; the brothers shared a mansion in Changxing Lane with three halberds at the gate—sixteen for a duke's household, twelve for first- and third-rank—outshining their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 嶧位終蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi ended his career as Prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ended his career as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 峴，樂善下士，少有吏幹。

translations.literal: Xian delighted in goodness and humbled himself before gentlemen; from youth he had talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: Xian delighted in virtue and treated scholars with respect; from youth he showed administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 以門廕入仕，累遷高陵令，政術知名。

translations.literal: He entered office through the privilege of his family's gate and was repeatedly promoted to Magistrate of Gaoling, renowned for governing skill.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through family privilege and rose to magistrate of Gaoling, famed for his governance.

sentences.zh: 特遷萬年令、河南少尹、魏郡太守；

translations.literal: He was specially transferred to Magistrate of Wannian, Vice Prefect of Henan, and Prefect of Wei Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to magistrate of Wannian, vice prefect of Henan, and prefect of Wei commandery;

sentences.zh: 入為金吾將軍，遷將作監，改京兆府尹，所在皆著聲績。

translations.literal: he entered as General of the Golden Chariots, was transferred to Director of Palace Construction, and changed to Prefect of Jingzhao—wherever he served he left noted reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: then entered as general of the golden chariots, became director of palace construction, and prefect of Jingzhao—winning renown wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，連雨六十余日，宰臣楊國忠惡其不附己，以雨災歸咎京兆尹，乃出為長沙郡太守。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao rain fell for more than sixty days; Chief Minister Yang Guozhong, disliking that he did not attach to him, blamed the rain disaster on the Prefect of Jingzhao and sent him out as Prefect of Changsha Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 754 rain fell for more than sixty days; Chief Minister Yang Guozhong, who disliked his independence, blamed the disaster on the Jingzhao prefect and exiled him as prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 時京師米麥踴貴，百姓謠曰：「欲得米粟賤，無過追李峴。

translations.literal: At that time grain and wheat in the capital soared in price; the people sang: "If you want rice and grain cheap, nothing surpasses recalling Li Xian."
translations.idiomatic: Grain prices in the capital soared; the people sang: "If you want cheap grain, nothing beats bringing back Li Xian."

sentences.zh: 」其為政得人心如此。

translations.literal: " Such was how his governance won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem his governance commanded.

sentences.zh: 至德初，朝廷務收才傑，以清寇難，峴召至行在，拜扶風太守、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide the court strove to gather outstanding talent to clear bandit troubles; Xian was summoned to the mobile court and appointed Prefect of Fufeng and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide reign the court sought outstanding men to quell rebellion; Xian was summoned to the mobile court as prefect of Fufeng and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至德二年十二月，制曰：「銀青光祿大夫、守禮部尚書李峴，饋軍周給，開物成務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide an edict stated: "Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Rites Li Xian—supplying the army comprehensively, opening affairs and completing tasks."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 757 an edict read: "Silver-gleaming grand master, acting minister of rites Li Xian has supplied the armies fully and advanced the state's business."

sentences.zh: 可光祿大夫，行御史大夫，兼京兆尹，封梁國公。

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Censor-in-Chief, concurrent Prefect of Jingzhao, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed grand master of splendid happiness, acting censor-in-chief, concurrent prefect of Jingzhao, and Duke of Liang."

sentences.zh: 」乾元二年，制曰：「李峴朝廷碩德，宗室藎臣。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Qianyuan an edict stated: "Li Xian is a great virtue of the court and a loyal minister of the imperial clan."
translations.idiomatic: " In 759 an edict declared: "Li Xian is a pillar of the court and a loyal minister of the imperial house."

sentences.zh: 可中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He may be Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed vice director of the secretariat and associate grand counselor."

sentences.zh: 」與呂諲、李揆、第五锜同拜相。

translations.literal: " He was appointed chief minister together with Lü Yin, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed chief minister together with Lü Yin, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi.

sentences.zh: 峴位望稍高，軍國大事，諸公莫敢言，皆獨決於峴，由是諲等銜之。

translations.literal: Xian's position and prestige were somewhat higher; on great affairs of army and state the others dared not speak and all were decided by Xian alone; thereby Yin and the others harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's standing was somewhat higher; on military and state affairs the other ministers dared not speak, and he decided alone—wherefore Yin and the others resented him.

sentences.zh: 初，李輔國判行軍司馬，潛令官軍於人間聽察是非，謂之察事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Fuguo acted as campaigning marshal and secretly ordered government troops to listen among the people for right and wrong, calling it "inspection affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Fuguo served as campaigning marshal and secretly ordered troops to spy on the populace, calling it "inspection affairs."

sentences.zh: 忠良被誣構者繼有之，須有追呼，諸司莫敢抗。

translations.literal: Loyal men framed in succession had to answer summons; no office dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men were framed one after another; when summons came no agency dared resist.

sentences.zh: 御史臺、大理寺重囚在獄，推斷未了，牒追就銀臺，不問輕重，一時釋放，莫敢違者。

translations.literal: Heavy prisoners in the Censorate and Court of Judicial Review, their cases not yet concluded, were summoned by writ to the Silver Terrace; regardless of severity they were released at once, and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Serious prisoners in the censorate and court of judicial review, trials unfinished, were summoned to the Silver Terrace and released regardless of gravity; none dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 每日於銀臺門決天下事，須處分，便稱制敕，禁中符印，悉佩之出入。

translations.literal: Each day at the Silver Terrace Gate he decided affairs of the realm; whatever required disposition he called an edict; palace seals and tallies he wore in going out and coming in.
translations.idiomatic: Each day at the Silver Terrace Gate he decided state affairs; whatever required action he called an edict; he carried palace seals in and out at will.

sentences.zh: 縱有敕，輔國押署，然後施行。

translations.literal: Even when there was an edict, Fuguo countersigned it before it could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Even genuine edicts required Fuguo's countersignature before execution.

sentences.zh: 及峴為相，叩頭論輔國專權亂國，上悟，賞峴正直，事並變革。

translations.literal: When Xian became chief minister he kowtowed and argued that Fuguo monopolized power and disturbed the state; the emperor understood, rewarded Xian's uprightness, and all matters were reformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian became chief minister he kowtowed and denounced Fuguo's monopoly of power; the emperor took heed, praised Xian's integrity, and reforms followed.

sentences.zh: 輔國以此讓行軍司馬，請歸本官，察事等並停，由是深怨峴。

translations.literal: Fuguo therefore yielded the campaigning marshal post and requested return to his original office; inspection affairs and the like were all stopped; thereby he deeply resented Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo yielded the campaigning marshal post, sought his former office, and inspection affairs ceased; he deeply resented Xian.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔七馬坊押官，先頗為盜，劫掠平人，州縣不能制，天興縣令知捕賊謝夷甫擒獲決殺之。

translations.literal: A custodian of Fengxiang's Seven Horse Stables had long been a robber, plundering common people; prefectures and counties could not control him. The Tianxing magistrate, knowing how to capture bandits, Xie Yifu, seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: A custodian of Fengxiang's Seven Horse Stables had long robbed and plundered civilians beyond local control; Tianxing magistrate Xie Yifu, skilled in apprehending bandits, seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 其妻進狀訴夫冤。

translations.literal: His wife submitted a petition alleging her husband's wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife petitioned the throne alleging wrongful execution.

sentences.zh: 輔國先為飛龍使，黨其人，為之上訴，詔監察御史孫鎣推之。

translations.literal: Fuguo had earlier been commissioner of the Flying Dragon Office and factionalized with the man; he appealed on his behalf, and an edict ordered Supervisory Censor Sun Jin to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo, formerly commissioner of the Flying Dragon Office, was the man's patron and appealed for him; the throne ordered supervisory censor Sun Jin to investigate.

sentences.zh: 鎣初直其事。

translations.literal: Jin at first upheld the case as just.
translations.idiomatic: Jin initially upheld the execution as lawful.

sentences.zh: 其妻又訴，詔令御史中丞崔伯陽、刑部侍郎李曄、大理卿權獻三司訊之，三司與鎣同。

translations.literal: His wife appealed again; an edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Boyang, Vice Minister of Justice Li Ye, and Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Quan Xian—the three offices—to examine it; the three offices agreed with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: She appealed again; Vice censor-in-chief Cui Boyang, vice minister of justice Li Ye, and chief justice Quan Xian were ordered to re-examine the case; all three agreed with Jin.

sentences.zh: 妻論訴不已，詔令侍御史毛若虛覆之，若虛歸罪於夷甫，又言伯陽等有情，不能質定刑獄。

translations.literal: The wife argued and appealed without cease; an edict ordered Attendant Censor Mao Ruoxu to review it. Ruoxu blamed Yifu and also said Boyang and the others were partial and could not determine criminal judgment.
translations.idiomatic: She kept appealing; attendant censor Mao Ruoxu was ordered to review the case; Ruoxu blamed Yifu and claimed Boyang and the others were partial and could not settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 伯陽怒，使人召若虛，詞氣不順。

translations.literal: Boyang was angry and sent someone to summon Ruoxu; his tone was not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang grew angry and summoned Ruoxu with harsh words.

sentences.zh: 伯陽欲上言之，若虛先馳謁，告急於肅宗，云：「已知，卿出去。

translations.literal: Boyang wished to report upward; Ruoxu first galloped to audience and cried urgency to Emperor Suzong, saying: "I know already—leave, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Before Boyang could report upward, Ruoxu raced to audience and cried urgency to Suzong, who said: "I know—leave."

sentences.zh: 」若虛奏曰：「臣出即死。

translations.literal: " Ruoxu memorialized: "If I go out I die at once."
translations.idiomatic: " Ruoxu replied: "If I leave, I die at once."

sentences.zh: 」上因留在簾內。

translations.literal: " The emperor therefore kept him inside the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor kept him within the curtain.

sentences.zh: 有頃，伯陽至，上問之，伯陽頗言若虛順旨，附會中人。

translations.literal: After a while Boyang arrived; the emperor questioned him, and Boyang largely said Ruoxu followed intent and attached to the inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Boyang arrived; questioned, he said Ruoxu curried favor and colluded with the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 上怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger ordered him out.

sentences.zh: 伯陽貶端州高要尉，權獻郴州桂陽尉，鳳翔尹嚴向及李曄皆貶嶺下一尉，鎣除名長流播州。

translations.literal: Boyang was demoted to Military Advisor of Gaoyao in Duan Prefecture; Quan Xian to Military Advisor of Guiyang in Chen Prefecture; Fengxiang Prefect Yan Xiang and Li Ye were all demoted to military advisors south of the mountains; Jin was struck from the rolls and exiled far to Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was demoted to military advisor of Gaoyao in Duan; Quan Xian to Guiyang in Chen; Fengxiang prefect Yan Xiang and Li Ye to posts south of the mountains; Jin was struck from the rolls and exiled to Bo.

sentences.zh: 峴以數人鹹非其罪，所責太重，欲理之，遂奏：「若虛希旨用刑，不守國法，陛下若信之重輕，是無御史臺。

translations.literal: Xian, considering that several men were all not guilty of their crimes and the penalties too heavy, wished to set matters right and memorialized: "Ruoxu follows intent in applying punishment and does not keep state law; if Your Majesty trusts his weighting of severity, there is no Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: Xian, believing several men were innocent and punished too harshly, memorialized: "Ruoxu applies punishment to please others and violates the law; if Your Majesty trusts his judgment of guilt, the censorate has no meaning."

sentences.zh: 」上怒峴言，出峴為蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry at Xian's words and sent Xian out as Prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Angered by Xian's words, the emperor sent him out as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 時右散騎常侍韓擇木入對，上謂之曰：「峴欲專權耶？

translations.literal: At that time Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Domestic Service Han Zemu entered for audience; the emperor said to him: "Does Xian wish to monopolize power?"
translations.idiomatic: When Right Regular Attendant Han Zemu attended audience, the emperor said to him: "Does Xian wish to monopolize power?"

sentences.zh: 何乃雲任毛若虛是無御史臺也？

translations.literal: Why does he say that trusting Mao Ruoxu means there is no Censorate?"
translations.idiomatic: Why does he say that trusting Mao Ruoxu means there is no censorate?"

sentences.zh: 令貶蜀州刺史，朕自覺用法太寬。

translations.literal: I ordered him demoted to Prefect of Shu Prefecture; I myself feel my application of law was too lenient."
translations.idiomatic: I demoted him to prefect of Shu; I myself see that my use of the law was too lenient."

sentences.zh: 」擇木對曰：「峴言直，非專權。

translations.literal: " Zemu replied: "Xian's words are direct, not a monopoly of power."
translations.idiomatic: " Zemu replied: "Xian spoke plainly, not from a wish to monopolize power."

sentences.zh: 陛下寬之，祗益聖德爾。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is lenient toward him, it only adds to sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is lenient with him, that only adds to your sagely virtue."

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，征峴為荊南節度、江陵尹，知江淮選補使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Xian was summoned as Military Commissioner of Jingnan, Prefect of Jiangling, and overseer of selection and appointment for the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong acceded, Xian was summoned as Jingnan military commissioner and prefect of Jiangling, with charge over Jiang-Huai selection and appointments.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部尚書，兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Rites and concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as minister of rites and concurrent director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 屬鑾輿幸陜，峴由商山路赴行在。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Shan, Xian took the Shangshan road to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Shan, Xian took the Shangshan route to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 既還京師，拜峴為黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Once the capital was restored, Xian was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to the capital he was appointed vice director of the secretariat and associate grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰臣不於政事堂邀客，時海內多務，宰相元載等見中官傳詔命至中書者，引之升政事堂，仍置榻待之；

translations.literal: By precedent chief ministers did not receive guests in the Hall of Administration of Affairs; at that time affairs were many throughout the realm, and chief ministers such as Yuan Zai, seeing palace eunuchs who came to the Secretariat bearing edicts, would lead them up into the Hall and still set out couches to receive them;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent chief ministers did not entertain guests in the Hall of Administration; with affairs pressing everywhere, Yuan Zai and other chief ministers, when eunuchs arrived at the Secretariat bearing edicts, would escort them into the hall and set out couches for them;

sentences.zh: 峴為宰相，令去其榻。

translations.literal: when Xian became chief minister he ordered the couches removed.
translations.idiomatic: when Xian became chief minister he ordered those couches removed.

sentences.zh: 奏請常參官各舉堪任諫官、憲官者，不限人數。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that each official attending regular audience recommend men fit to serve as remonstrating officials or censorial officials, with no limit on number.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that each official in regular audience recommend men fit for remonstrating or censorial office, without limit on number.

sentences.zh: 初收東京，受偽官陳希烈已下數百人，崔器希旨深刻，奏皆處死；

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was first recovered, several hundred false officials from Chen Xilie downward were taken; Cui Qi, following intent with harsh severity, memorialized that all be put to death;
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was first recovered, several hundred collaborators from Chen Xilie downward were taken; Cui Qi, eager to please with harsh severity, memorialized that all be executed;

sentences.zh: 上意亦欲懲勸天下，欲從器議。

translations.literal: the emperor's mind also wished to warn and instruct the realm and was inclined to follow Qi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also wished to warn the realm and was inclined to follow Qi's proposal.

sentences.zh: 時峴為三司使，執之曰：「夫事有首從，情有輕重，若一概處死，恐非陛下含弘之義，又失國家惟新之典。
