translations.literal: At that time Xian was commissioner of the three offices and held fast, saying: "Affairs have leaders and followers, circumstances have light and heavy; if all are put to death alike, I fear that is not Your Majesty's meaning of inclusive magnanimity, and it also loses the state's rite of renewal."
translations.idiomatic: Xian, then commissioner of the three offices, objected: "Crimes have leaders and followers, guilt has degrees of severity; to execute all alike would betray Your Majesty's magnanimity and the state's rite of renewal."

sentences.zh: 且羯胡亂常，無不淩據，二京全陷，萬乘南巡，各顧其生，衣冠蕩覆。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jie barbarians disturbed the norm and everywhere overran and seized; both capitals fell entirely, the Son of Heaven toured south, each cared for his life, and officials and gentry were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels overran the realm, both capitals fell, the emperor fled south, and each man sought to survive—officials and gentry were swept away.

sentences.zh: 或陛下親戚，或勛舊子孫，皆置極法，恐乖仁恕之旨。

translations.literal: Some are Your Majesty's kin, some are sons and grandsons of meritorious ministers—if all are subjected to extreme law, I fear it strays from the purpose of benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Some are Your Majesty's kin, some descendants of meritorious ministers—to punish all with the utmost penalty would betray benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 昔者明王用刑，殲厥渠魁，脅從罔理。

translations.literal: In antiquity enlightened kings used punishment to destroy the ringleaders; coerced followers were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Enlightened kings of old punished only the ringleaders; coerced followers went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 況河北殘寇未平，官吏多陷，茍容漏網，適開自新之路，若盡行誅，是堅叛逆之黨，誰人更圖效順？

translations.literal: Moreover bandits in Hebei are not yet pacified and many officials are implicated; if we tolerate those who slip through the net, we open the road to renewal—if all are executed, we harden the party of rebellion; who would then seek to submit?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover rebels in Hebei are not yet subdued and many officials were implicated; sparing those who escaped the net opens the path to renewal—mass execution would harden the rebels; who would then submit?

sentences.zh: 困獸猶鬥，況數萬人乎！

translations.literal: A cornered beast still fights—how much more tens of thousands of men!
translations.idiomatic: A cornered beast still fights—how much more so tens of thousands of men!

sentences.zh: 」崔器、呂諲，皆守文之吏，不識大體，殊無變通。

translations.literal: " Cui Qi and Lü Yin were both officials who clung to the letter of the law, did not grasp the larger pattern, and were wholly without flexibility.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Qi and Lü Yin were sticklers for the letter of the law who grasped neither the larger pattern nor flexible judgment.

sentences.zh: 廷議數日，方從峴奏，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Court debate lasted several days before Xian's memorial was followed; very many were wholly spared.
translations.idiomatic: After days of court debate the throne followed Xian's memorial, and a great many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 其料敵決事皆此類。

translations.literal: His assessing enemies and deciding affairs were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment of affairs was characteristically of this sort.

sentences.zh: 竟為中官所擠，罷知政事，為太子詹事，尋遷吏部尚書，知江淮舉選，置銓洪州。

translations.literal: In the end he was squeezed out by palace eunuchs, ceased handling government affairs, became Household Administrator to the Heir Apparent, and soon was transferred to Minister of Personnel, overseeing Jiang-Huai examination selection, with accreditation set at Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was ultimately forced out by palace eunuchs, left the chief ministry, became household administrator to the heir apparent, then minister of personnel overseeing Jiang-Huai examinations, with accreditation at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，改檢校兵部尚書，兼衢州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to acting Minister of War and concurrent Prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became acting minister of war and concurrent prefect of Qu.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年七月以疾終，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yongtai he died of illness at fifty-eight years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 766 he died of illness at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 李巨，曾祖父虢王鳳，高祖之第十四子也。

translations.literal: Li Ju's great-grandfather was Prince of Guo Li Feng, the fourteenth son of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju's great-grandfather was Prince of Guo Li Feng, the fourteenth son of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 鳳孫邕，嗣虢王，巨即邕之第二子也。

translations.literal: Feng's grandson Yong succeeded to the title Prince of Guo; Ju was Yong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's grandson Yong succeeded as Prince of Guo; Ju was Yong's second son.

sentences.zh: 剛銳果決，頗涉獵書史，好屬文。

translations.literal: He was firm, sharp, resolute, and decisive; he ranged widely through books and histories and delighted in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Firm, sharp, and decisive, he read widely in history and delighted in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 開元中為嗣虢王。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan he was heir to the Prince of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he was heir to the Prince of Guo.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，出為西河太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao he went out as Prefect of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: In 746 he was appointed prefect of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 皇太子杜良娣之妹婿柳勣陷詔獄，巨母扶余氏，吉溫嫡母之妹也，溫為京兆士曹，推勣之黨，以徐征等往來巨家，資給之，由是坐貶義陽郡司馬。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's consort Du Liangdi's sister's husband Liu Ji fell into the imperial prison; Ju's mother was the Fu Yu clan—Ji Wen's legal mother's younger sister. Wen was a staff officer of Jingzhao; pursuing Ji's faction, he cited Xu Zheng and others coming and going to Ju's household and supplying him, and thereby Ju was demoted as punishment to Military Advisor of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince's consort Du Liangdi's brother-in-law Liu Ji was imprisoned, Ju's mother Lady Fu was a younger sister of Ji Wen's stepmother; Wen, a Jingzhao staff officer, traced Ji's faction through Xu Zheng's visits and support to Ju's household, and Ju was demoted to military advisor of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 六載，御史中丞楊慎矜為李林甫、王鉷構陷得罪，其黨史敬忠亦伏法。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin was framed by Li Linfu and Wang Hong and punished; his partisan Shi Jingzhong also suffered the law.
translations.idiomatic: In 747 vice censor-in-chief Yang Shenjin was framed by Li Linfu and Wang Hong; his associate Shi Jingzhong was also executed.

sentences.zh: 以巨與敬忠相識，坐解官，於南賓郡安置。

translations.literal: Because Ju knew Jingzhong, he was punished by removal from office and settled in Nanbin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ju knew Jingzhong, he was dismissed and settled in Nanbin commandery.

sentences.zh: 又起為夷陵郡太守。

translations.literal: He was again raised as Prefect of Yiling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as prefect of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 及祿山陷東京，玄宗方擇將帥，張垍言巨善騎射，有謀略，玄宗追至京師。

translations.literal: When Lushan took the Eastern Capital, Emperor Xuanzong was selecting generals; Zhang Yan said Ju was skilled at riding and archery and had strategy, and Xuanzong summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan took the Eastern Capital, Xuanzong was choosing generals; Zhang Yan praised Ju's horsemanship, archery, and strategy, and the emperor summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠素與巨相識，忌之，謂人曰：「如此小兒，豈得令見人主！

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong had long known Ju and resented him, saying to others: "Such a stripling—how can he be allowed to see the sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, who knew Ju well, resented him and said: "Such a stripling—how can he be allowed before the throne!"

sentences.zh: 」經月余日不得見。

translations.literal: " For more than a month he could not obtain audience.
translations.idiomatic: " For more than a month he was denied audience.

sentences.zh: 玄宗使中官召入奏事，玄宗大悅，遂令中官劉奉庭宣敕令宰相與巨語，幾亭午，方出。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had a palace eunuch summon him to report; Xuanzong was greatly pleased and then ordered the eunuch Liu Fengting to proclaim an edict directing the chief ministers to speak with Ju; it was nearly noon before he came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had a eunuch summon him to report; greatly pleased, he ordered Liu Fengting to direct the chief ministers to confer with Ju; Ju did not emerge until nearly noon.

sentences.zh: 國忠頗怠，對奉庭謂巨曰：「比來人多口打賊，公不爾乎？

translations.literal: Guozhong was rather indolent; facing Fengting he said to Ju: "Lately many people only talk of fighting the rebels with their mouths—are you not like that?"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong, indifferent, said to Ju before Fengting: "Lately everyone only talks of fighting rebels—are you not the same?"

sentences.zh: 」巨曰：「不知若個軍將能與相公手打賊乎？

translations.literal: " Ju said: "I do not know which army officer could fight rebels hand to hand with the Chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: " Ju replied: "Which general, I wonder, could fight rebels hand to hand with the chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 」尋授陳留譙郡太守、攝御史大夫、河南節度使。

translations.literal: " Soon he was appointed Prefect of Chenliu and Qiao Commanderies, acting Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon appointed prefect of Chenliu and Qiao, acting censor-in-chief, and Henan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 翌日，巨稱官銜奉謝，玄宗驚曰：「何得令攝？

translations.literal: The next day Ju gave thanks using the title "acting"; Xuanzong was startled and said: "How could he be made acting?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ju gave thanks as "acting" censor-in-chief; Xuanzong exclaimed: "Why was he only acting?"

sentences.zh: 」即日詔兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: " That same day an edict made him concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day an edict appointed him concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 巨奏曰：「方今艱難，恐為賊所詐，如忽召臣，不知何以取信？

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: "The times are hard; I fear being deceived by rebels—if I am suddenly summoned, how am I to be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized: "These are desperate times; rebels may deceive us—if I am suddenly summoned, how will men trust me?"

sentences.zh: 」玄宗劈木契分授之，遂以臣兼統嶺南節度使何履光、黔中節度使趙國珍、南陽節度使魯炅，先領三節度事。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong split wooden tallies and gave portions to him; thus he was made to oversee concurrently the Lingnan Military Commissioner He Luguang, the Qianzhong Military Commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and the Nanyang Military Commissioner Lu Hui, first taking charge of the three commissions' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong split wooden tallies and gave him portions; he was charged to oversee Lingnan commissioner He Luguang, Qianzhong commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and Nanyang commissioner Lu Hui, first taking command of all three.

sentences.zh: 有詔貶炅為果毅，以潁川太守來瑱兼御史中丞代之。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Hui to resolute cavalry officer and had Yingchuan Prefect Lai Tian replace him as concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Hui to resolute cavalry officer and appointed Yingchuan prefect Lai Tian concurrent vice censor-in-chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 巨奏曰：「若炅能存孤城，其功足以補過，則何以處之？

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: "If Hui can preserve the isolated city, his merit is enough to offset fault—then how is he to be treated?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju asked: "If Hui can hold the isolated city, his merit may offset his fault—how then should he be treated?"

sentences.zh: 」玄宗曰：「卿隨宜處置之。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong said: "You may dispose as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong said: "Dispose of it as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 」巨至內鄉，趣南陽，賊將畢思琛聞之，解圍走。

translations.literal: " Ju reached Neixiang and hastened to Nanyang; the rebel general Bi Sichen heard of it and lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju reached Neixiang and pressed on to Nanyang; rebel general Bi Sichen heard and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 巨趣何履光、趙國珍同至南陽，宣敕貶炅，削其章服，令隨軍效力。

translations.literal: Ju urged He Luguang and Zhao Guozhen to come together to Nanyang, proclaimed the edict demoting Hui, stripped his insignia and robes, and ordered him to serve with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ju summoned He Luguang and Zhao Guozhen to Nanyang, proclaimed Hui's demotion, stripped his insignia, and ordered him to serve with the army.

sentences.zh: 至日晚，以恩命令炅復位。

translations.literal: By evening, by grace he ordered Hui restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: By evening he graciously restored Hui to office.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，為太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 757 he became junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十月，收西京，為留守、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Western Capital was recovered; he served as Defender and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, when the Western Capital was recovered, he served as defender and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年夏四月，加太子少師、兼河南尹，充東京留守，判尚書省事，充東畿采訪等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the third year he was given Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, concurrent Prefect of Henan, charged as Defender of the Eastern Capital, judged affairs of the Department of State Affairs, and charged as Investigation Commissioner of the Eastern Metropolitan Region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 758 he was made junior tutor to the heir apparent, concurrent prefect of Henan, defender of the Eastern Capital, with charge over the department of state affairs and investigation commissioner of the eastern metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 於城市橋梁稅出入車牛等錢以供國用，頗有幹沒，士庶怨讟。

translations.literal: On city bridges he taxed money on carts, oxen, and the like entering and leaving to supply state use; there was considerable embezzlement, and scholars and commoners resented and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: He levied bridge tolls on carts and livestock entering the city to supply state revenue, embezzled heavily, and drew popular resentment.

sentences.zh: 後與妃張氏不睦，張氏即皇后從父妹也。

translations.literal: Later he was not harmonious with his consort the Zhang clan—Zhang was the empress's paternal cousin's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Later he quarreled with his consort Lady Zhang, the empress's cousin.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿李遵構之，發其所犯贓賄，貶為遂州刺史。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Court Li Zun framed him, exposed his bribery offenses, and he was demoted to Prefect of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clan director Li Zun framed him, exposed his bribery, and he was demoted to prefect of Su.

sentences.zh: 屬劍南東川節度兵馬使、梓州刺史段子璋反，以眾襲節度使李奐於綿州，路經遂州，巨蒼黃修屬郡禮迎之，為子璋所殺。

translations.literal: When the military commissioner of the eastern circuit of Jiannan, Prefect of Zi Prefecture Duan Zizhang, rebelled and with troops attacked Military Commissioner Li Huan at Mian Prefecture, passing through Su Prefecture, Ju in haste had his subordinates prepare the prefecture's rites to welcome him and was killed by Zizhang.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Jiannan military commissioner and Zi prefect Duan Zizhang rebelled and attacked commissioner Li Huan at Mian, passing through Su, Ju hastily had his staff prepare a ceremonial welcome and was killed by Zizhang.

sentences.zh: 子則之，以宗室歷官，好學，年五十余，每執經詣太學聽受。

translations.literal: His son Zhezhi, through the imperial clan serving in office, loved learning; past fifty, each time he held the classics he went to the Imperial Academy to listen and receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhezhi, a clansman in office who loved learning, still in his fifties went regularly to the Imperial Academy with classics in hand to hear lectures.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王臯自荊南來朝，稱薦之，貞元二年，自睦王府長史遷左金吾衛大將軍，以從父甥竇申追遊無閑親累，貶昭州司馬。

translations.literal: Heir to Prince of Cao Li Gao, coming from Jingnan to court, praised and recommended him; in the second year of Zhenyuan, from Chief Administrator of the Mansion of Prince of Mu he was transferred to General of the Left Golden Chariots Guard; because his cousin on the father's side Dou Shen pursued pleasure without leisure and implicated kin, he was demoted to Military Advisor of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Heir to Prince of Cao Li Gao, arriving from Jingnan, recommended him; in 786 he rose from chief administrator of the Prince of Mu's mansion to general of the Left Golden Chariots Guard; implicated by his cousin Dou Shen's dissolute companionship, he was demoted to military advisor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：暠孝友清慎，居官有稱；

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Gao was filial, friendly, pure, and cautious, and in office had a reputation;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Gao was filial, friendly, pure, and cautious, and won repute in office;

sentences.zh: 齊物貞廉整肅，復節制權謀；

translations.literal: Qi Wu was upright, incorruptible, stern, and orderly; Fu controlled power and stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was upright, incorruptible, and stern; Fu exercised command with shrewd stratagem;

sentences.zh: 國貞清白守法，皆神通之曾玄，宗室之翹楚。

translations.literal: Guozhen was pure, white, and law-abiding—all were great-grandsons and great-great-grandsons of Shentong, outstanding men of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was pure and law-abiding—all were descendants of Shentong, outstanding men of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 锜之為逆，不累其親，前人之積德彰矣，當朝之用法明矣。

translations.literal: Qi's rebellion did not implicate his kin; the accumulated virtue of forebears was manifest, and the present court's application of law was clear.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's rebellion did not implicate his kin—the virtue of forebears shone clear, and the court's use of law was manifest.

sentences.zh: 然暠發人陰私，齊物積財興議，國貞急於操下，皆尺之短也。

translations.literal: Yet Gao exposed people's hidden affairs, Qi Wu amassed wealth and stirred debate, and Guozhen was urgent in controlling subordinates—all were a foot's short measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gao exposed private misconduct, Qi Wu amassed wealth and drew criticism, and Guozhen was harsh with subordinates—these were their flaws.

sentences.zh: 麟修整，峘循良，匪躬立事，始終無玷者，皆宗室之英也。

translations.literal: Lin was cultivated and orderly, Huan followed the good path; those who devoted themselves without self and stood in affairs, without stain from beginning to end, were all heroes of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was cultivated, Huan dutiful and capable; those who devoted themselves to office without stain from start to finish were all eminent clansmen.

sentences.zh: 峴之剛正才略，有足可稱。

translations.literal: Xian's firm uprightness and talent in strategy had enough to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's firm integrity and strategic talent deserve praise.

sentences.zh: 初為國忠所憎，終沮朝恩之勢。

translations.literal: At first hated by Guozhong, in the end he checked the power of court favor.
translations.idiomatic: Hated first by Guozhong, he ultimately checked the power of court favoritism.

sentences.zh: 處群邪之內，堅獨正之心，是不吐也；

translations.literal: Amid a host of wicked men he kept a solitary upright heart—this is not yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Among the wicked he kept an upright heart alone—he would not yield;

sentences.zh: 活東都之命，是不茹也。

translations.literal: he spared the lives of the Eastern Capital—this is not swallowing injustice.
translations.idiomatic: he spared the lives of the Eastern Capital—he would not swallow injustice.

sentences.zh: 庶幾乎仲山甫之道焉！

translations.literal: He may be compared to the way of Zhong Shanfu!
translations.idiomatic: He approached the way of Zhong Shanfu!

sentences.zh: 巨以剛銳果決，亦可嘉焉，終以贓賄貪殘，良可痛也。

translations.literal: Ju, for his firmness, sharpness, and resolve, is also praiseworthy; yet in the end, for bribery, greed, and cruelty, it is truly painful.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's firmness and resolve were admirable; yet his bribery, greed, and cruelty are truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宗室賢良，枝葉茂盛。

translations.literal: The encomium states: The imperial clan is worthy and good; branches and leaves flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The imperial clan is worthy; its branches flourish.

sentences.zh: 最尤者誰？

translations.literal: Who is most outstanding?
translations.idiomatic: Who stands highest among them?

sentences.zh: 峴獨守正。

translations.literal: Xian alone keeps to the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xian alone held to the upright path.
